In previous years, safety tests were probably conducted once a year and were simple. Equipment Owners sign a tick record form that states that the test performed actually passed the test. This method of conducting tests is known as Visual Testing, which can help early identify obvious electrical problems (e.g., damaged sockets, frayed plugs, plugs stuck in the socket). Nevertheless, visual inspection alone can't find less visible problems, such as aging leads, loose hooks, and damaged provision wires in the artwork, and these problems can only exist through more detailed testing.
